text: A line from a node to a gateway is an upload, not a radio link. The packet may have crossed several relays on the way, and their route is not recorded.
Every mark flies for the same time, whatever the distance. Speed is not data: each gateway stamps its own clock, so latency cannot be measured.
Heard by it, as a gateway
The two are never added together, and neither is a scale you can read a number off. A gateway carrying other people’s traffic is not a node with a lot to say.
Uploads, not listeners. Only a gateway reports, so a node that heard a packet and did not upload it is invisible here. A "+N" beside a sender counts the gateways whose arcs are not drawn.
No measured noise floor in this reading.
Dots are nodes, coloured by role. The role key under the map filters them.

How often each node sends, against the firmware defaults. A node that keeps announcing itself is usually restarting, and a node that keeps restarting usually needs power rather than a change of settings. Counts include packets sent on boot and in reply to a request, so read this as a reason to ask, not as a verdict.

MQTT sends this node’s traffic to a server over the internet, so the mesh can be seen on a map and from other sites. It is optional and the node works without it. Credentials for the community broker come from the AZ Meshtastic Discord.
Optional: connect this node to the azmsh.net MQTT broker, or change a recommended value
Reads the configuration straight off the node, so there is no export step. Nothing is sent anywhere — the config stays in this browser, including the channel keys and any MQTT password.
